Es el precio de una moneda en otra. En l: It is the price of one currency in another. In the eurozone it is given as the ECB publishes it: $E$ units of the other currency per €1 (for example, €1 = $1.08). To convert euros into the other currency you multiply by $E$ and to go back to euros you divide. If $E$ rises, the euro appreciates (is worth more) and the other currency depreciates.
Si se conoce el valor del euro en dos mo: If the value of the euro in two currencies is known, the rate between them comes from dividing: with €1 = $1.08 and €1 = £0.85, one dollar is worth 0.85/1.08 = 0.787 pounds. This is how rates are calculated between currencies that are not quoted directly.
La PPA dice que, a largo plazo, el mismo: PPP says that, in the long run, the same good should cost the same everywhere, so the exchange rate would be $E_{PPP} = P_f/P$. The real exchange rate, $q = E · P/P_f$, counts how many foreign goods can be bought with what one costs here: if it is greater than 1, the euro is overvalued. The Big Mac index from The Economist compares the price of the burger in each country this way.
Aunque los niveles de precios no se igua: Even if price levels do not equalize, the relative version says the exchange rate offsets the inflation difference: $E_1 = E_0 · (1 + π_f)/(1 + π)$. The currency of the country with higher inflation depreciates, approximately, by the difference between the two inflation rates.
